summary.name: SizeUp
summary.one_liner: SizeUp is a keyboard-driven macOS window manager that resizes and positions the frontmost window using predefined actions and shortcuts.
use_cases: Put two windows side by side for comparison
Snap a window to a screen half or quarter
Keep space at screen edges for desktop icons
Add gaps between windows to avoid shadow overlap
summary.what_it_does: SizeUp moves and resizes the frontmost window of almost any Mac application using a set of predefined actions. It can fill the left, right, top, or bottom half of the screen, or a quarter (quadrant) of the screen. It can reserve space at the screen edges, for example to keep access to desktop icons. It can also add distance between windows to avoid shadow overlap. The page describes it as shortcut-driven, and the listing calls it keyboard-centric.
notable: Predefined half-screen and quadrant window placements
Reserves screen edge space for desktop icon access
Adds gaps between windows to avoid shadow overlap
caveats: Page does not state pricing or whether it is free or paid
Page does not give a version, release date, or minimum macOS version
Page describes Mac OS X generally; current macOS compatibility is not stated
